title: Patani Kingdom
capsule: Patani (Patani Darussalam) was a Malay Muslim sultanate on the eastern shore of the Malay Peninsula, in the region of present-day Pattani Province in southern Thailand. During this period it flourished as one of the great entrepôts of the South China Sea, drawing Chinese, Japanese, Javanese, Portuguese, and Dutch traders; the Dutch and English East India Companies both maintained factories there in the early seventeenth century. Its golden age fell under a succession of four ruling queens (raja perempuan) beginning with Raja Hijau in 1584, the most formidable of whom, Raja Ungu, repeatedly resisted the overlordship of Ayutthaya and inflicted a notable defeat on a Siamese invasion in 1634.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory around the Pattani River estuary is documented in Portuguese and Dutch trade records, but the northern and western boundaries of the sultanate's territorial claim are not precisely delimited in contemporary sources.
